explanations.silhouette:
Every sprite starts as a shape. Block in the whole potion in one flat color and ignore the detail for now. If the silhouette reads as a potion on its own, the finished sprite will too.

![Silhouette in one flat color](examples/silhouette.png) ![The finished potion](examples/finished.png)

The **Fill** tool is quickest: draw the edge with the **Pencil**, then fill inside it.
explanations.outline:
Draw the outline over the edge of the silhouette. Keep it **1 pixel wide**: where the line steps diagonally, pixels touch only at their corners, never side by side.

The lit left side of the glass uses a lighter blue than the right side and the bottom, so the outline already shows where the light comes from.

![The outline on its own](examples/outline.png)
explanations.base:
Base colors are the flat middle tones of each material: red for the liquid and tan for the cork. Most of this Step is already done, because you blocked the silhouette in red. Add the cork.

![Outline and base colors, no shading yet](examples/flat.png)
explanations.shadow:
Light comes from the top left, so shadow goes on the sides that face away from it: the right edge and bottom of the liquid, and the right half of the cork. A shadow is a darker version of its base color, not black.

![Flat](examples/flat.png) ![With shadow](examples/shaded.png)
explanations.highlight:
A highlight is the brightest color, used sparingly where the light hits hardest. A pale glint runs down the neck and catches the upper left of the glass. Those few pixels are what make it read as glass.

![With shadow](examples/shaded.png) ![With highlights](examples/finished.png)

The same outline, shadow and glint work for any potion:

![Three other potions from the same set](examples/other-potions.png)
